Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bayesfam (development version)

Breaking changes

  • lomax() now uses link_alpha = "logm1" by default; the old default was "log1p". The old link let alpha fall below 1, where the Lomax density is undefined. Code that calls lomax() without link_alpha now fits alpha on a different link scale, which changes its priors and coefficients; pass link_alpha = "log1p" to get the old behaviour.

Bug fixes

  • rlomax() now rejects alpha <= 1, like dlomax() and qlomax().
  • cauchitnormal(), cloglognormal(), logitnormal() and softplusnormal() no longer bound mu. It is the location of the normal variable before the transform, so it can take any real value.
  • dgompertz(), qgompertz(), dsoftplusnormal() and rsoftplusnormal() now reject a vector argument when any element of it is invalid, not only when all elements are; so do dlomax() and qlomax() for alpha.
  • dgompertz(), qgompertz(), rgompertz() and the Gompertz Stan code use expm1(), so they stay accurate when mu * beta is small; before, qgompertz(0.5, 1, 1e-16) gave 0 instead of the median 1.
  • runit_lindley() and the unit Lindley Stan RNG draw from a gamma mixture; for mu below about 0.0013 every draw was NaN.
  • rshifted_inv_gaussian(), rsimplex() and their Stan RNGs compute the smaller inverse Gaussian root without cancellation; for small shapes or large sigma, draws landed at or below the shift, or at 0.
  • inv_cloglog() uses expm1(), so it no longer rounds to 0 below x of about -37.
  • lomax() includes brms’ logm1 Stan functions only when link or link_alpha is "logm1".
  • cloglog() and cauchit() give their own name in their error messages; before, both said “logit link”.
  • The unit Lindley posterior_predict reads mu through brms::get_dpar().

New features

  • posterior_epred is now implemented for gompertz(), generalized_gamma(), cauchitnormal(), cloglognormal() and softplusnormal(). The generalized gamma mean is Inf where it does not exist, for Q * sigma <= -1, and stays accurate as Q approaches 0, down to the smallest normal double; for subnormal Q it overflows to Inf. The Gompertz mean stays finite where expm1(mu * beta) overflows, as long as the product mu * beta is itself finite.
  • unit_lindley(), generalized_gamma(), simplex(), shifted_inv_gaussian() and shifted_lognormal_uniform() now define a Stan _rng function.
  • dfrechet_median() gains a log argument.
